newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: US sees critical mass in Geneva telecoms talks.
newsitem.headline: US sees critical mass in Geneva telecoms talks.

text.p: U.S. Deputy Trade Representative Jeffrey Lang said on Saturday that a critical mass had been reached in the telecoms negotiations if other countries did not introduce any changes.

He told reporters "the U.S. saw a critical mass now reached", implying Washington was ready to sign up to a deal, but he cautioned that other countries would have to maintain their offers as they stood and not introduce any changes before Saturday's deadline.
Another U.S. official said there had been intensive discussions overnight with the Canadian negotiators, but there was no indication of the outcome of these talks.
Washington had strongly criticised Canada's offer restricting foreign equity ownership in its domestic telecoms companies.
The World Trade Organisation-sponsored negotiations face a midnight Geneva deadline (2300 GMT) for agreement.

On Friday, the U.S. said it was adding restrictions on transmission of some television and audio services to its offer on the table. But other trading powers made clear they were still ready for an accord and a U.S. official said there would be no extension of talks beyond February 15.
